item.title: Assistant Minister for Agriculture Inosi Kuridrani passes away
item.description: Assistant Minister for Agriculture, Waterways, and Sugar Industry Inosi Kuridrani has passed away. Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has confirmed in Parliament this morning that he passed away last night.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Minister for Agriculture, Waterways, and Sugar Industry Inosi Kuridrani has passed away.

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has confirmed in Parliament this morning that he passed away last night.

He extended his condolences to Kuridrani’s family and the Vanua.

Speaker of Parliament Filimone Jitoko also extended his condolences.

A moment of silence was also observed in Parliament.

Other Members of Parliament are also extending their condolences to the late Kuridrani’s family.

item.title: Mataiciwa urges media to ensure accurate and reliable election reporting
item.description: The media has an important role to play in ensuring voters have access to timely, accurate and reliable information during the electoral process. This has been highlighted by Supervisor of Elections Ana Mataiciwa while opening the Media and Elections Reporting Training at Communications Fiji Limited this morning.
item.content:encoded:
The media has an important role to play in ensuring voters have access to timely, accurate and reliable information during the electoral process.

This has been highlighted by Supervisor of Elections Ana Mataiciwa while opening the Media and Elections Reporting Training at Communications Fiji Limited this morning.

Mataiciwa says the media is one of the most important links between electoral processes and the public, helping voters understand how elections work, what is happening and where they can access verified information.

She says this influence comes with the responsibility to report accurately, fairly and impartially.

Mataiciwa says the training will cover the legal framework governing elections and the media’s role and responsibilities, as well as fact-checking and the growing challenges of misinformation and disinformation, including content generated through artificial intelligence.

She says the programme will also focus on inclusive election reporting, including equitable coverage of women and marginalised candidates and making election information accessible and relevant to Fiji’s diverse voter groups, including young people and those living in rural and maritime communities.

She says a professional and well-informed media is an important partner in ensuring voters have access to credible electoral information.

Mataiciwa says in an environment where information can travel across the country in seconds, misinformation can spread just as quickly, making accuracy more important than ever.

item.title: Missing cocaine exhibits a very serious issue - Naivalurua
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua , Rashika Kumar · 28/09/2026 Minister for Policing Ioane Naivalurua says the disappearance of cocaine exhibits that were kept in the custody of the Suva High Court is a very serious issue.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua , Rashika Kumar · 28/09/2026

Minister for Policing Ioane Naivalurua says the disappearance of cocaine exhibits that were kept in the custody of the Suva High Court is a very serious issue.

fijivillage News was alerted that cocaine from the case involving Joshua Aziz Rahman was allegedly missing from the Suva Court House.

We then sought clarification from Police and the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

The Office of the DPP informed us that it was not aware of the allegations, but advised that we check with Police, as they are responsible for exhibits, including the storage and security of drugs.

We were told last Monday that the drugs were not missing.

However, Assistant Commissioner of Police Crime Loraini Seru says a physical check of the exhibits was conducted on Tuesday in the presence of senior judiciary officials, a senior official from the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, Police, and an officer from Crime Scene Investigations, who documented the inspection process.

Naivalurua says the issue now is to find ways and means, or put a system in place, to ensure that this does not happen again.

Meanwhile, Minister for Justice and Acting Attorney General Siromi Turaga has given an assurance that a thorough, rigorous and completely independent criminal investigation has been initiated by the Criminal Investigations Department of the Fiji Police Force to establish the exact circumstances surrounding the disappearance of seven bars of cocaine from the Suva Court House exhibit room.

Turaga says he is deeply concerned by the reported tampering with and disappearance of cocaine exhibits.

As the Minister responsible for the administration of justice and upholding the rule of law, he says his absolute priority is ensuring that State systems are anchored in unwavering governance, strict accountability and proper statutory processes.

The Minister says he will not be directly involved in the operational timeline or specific directions of the inquiry.

H owever, he says his ministerial oversight is focused squarely on ensuring that the independent investigative bodies are fully resourced and completely unhindered, and that the robust legal processes governing evidence custody are upheld without fear or favour.

The Acting Attorney General says the proper handling, security and management of exhibits held by the courts are sacred institutional responsibilities, and any failure to adhere to established protocols must be treated with the utmost seriousness.

He says the public is entirely entitled to demand transparency and answers on a matter of such profound public interest.

item.title: TISI Sangam election didn't go ahead, interim committee to oversee affairs
item.description: The TISI Sangam election did not go ahead as scheduled today at Sangam College in Nadi, with National President Parveen Bala confirming that an Interim Committee has been nominated to oversee the organisation’s affairs for now. Bala and fellow presidential candidate Damend Gounder have nominated the Interim Committee, and a Council of Management meeting will be held soon to provide further directi
item.content:encoded:
The TISI Sangam election did not go ahead as scheduled today at Sangam College in Nadi, with National President Parveen Bala confirming that an Interim Committee has been nominated to oversee the organisation’s affairs for now.

Bala and fellow presidential candidate Damend Gounder have nominated the Interim Committee, and a Council of Management meeting will be held soon to provide further direction.

When questioned about the commotion during the election and Annual General Meeting, Bala told fijivillage News that heated arguments can be expected during a large gathering, but everything was under control.

Insert: Floor given to members 27th Sept

Some of the members publicly said they want the elections to go ahead.

Following a closed-door meeting, Bala and Gounder agreed to serve as co-chairs of the Interim Committee, with each expected to appoint seven members as interim executives.

The other presidential candidate, Dorsami Naidu, will also be included in the Interim Committee.

Earlier today, TISI Sangam members had been pushing for the elections to proceed as scheduled and not be delayed.

item.title: 19-year-old charged over alleged Nakasi temple break-in
item.description: A 19-year-old man charged in relation to an alleged sacrilege case will appear in the Nasinu Magistrates Court this morning. The accused, who resides in Wainibuku, is alleged to have broken into a temple in Nakasi on 11th of this month.
item.content:encoded:
A 19-year-old man charged in relation to an alleged sacrilege case will appear in the Nasinu Magistrates Court this morning.

The accused, who resides in Wainibuku, is alleged to have broken into a temple in Nakasi on 11th of this month.

He is alleged to have stolen money from the temple.

The accused has been charged with one count of sacrilege and one count of theft.

item.title: Mother recalls fear, sacrifice and joy as son beats blood cancer
item.description: Nazia Ali, mother of 14-year-old Hazrat Ali, remembers the devastation she felt 12 years ago when doctors first told her that her two-year-old son had blood cancer. Sharing her family’s experience during Gold September, which raises awareness about childhood cancer, Ali says her son’s symptoms included unexplained pain in his leg and a fever.
item.content:encoded:
Nazia Ali, mother of 14-year-old Hazrat Ali, remembers the devastation she felt 12 years ago when doctors first told her that her two-year-old son had blood cancer.

Sharing her family’s experience during Gold September, which raises awareness about childhood cancer, Ali says her son’s symptoms included unexplained pain in his leg and a fever.

She says her son is now 14 years old, healthy and cancer-free, but she still remembers how difficult it was to accept the diagnosis.

Ali says there is also a misconception that blood cancer only affects children who have a family history of the disease, stressing that this is not necessarily the case.

She says Hazrat began chemotherapy, she tried to make the frightening experience easier for him by telling him the treatment would turn him into a superhero.

However, behind those words of encouragement, Ali says she was scared after doctors told the family her son had a 50-50 chance.

She says instead of focusing on the possibility of losing him, she placed her faith in the positive 50 percent and continued to hope that he would recover.

Ali says she was also frightened when doctors warned that there was a high possibility of the cancer returning.

As a teacher, Ali took leave without pay so she could care for her son throughout his three years of treatment , most of which was carried out in Fiji.

After years of chemotherapy, uncertainty and sacrifice, the mother says one of the happiest moments for the family came when they were finally told that Hazrat was cancer-free.
